title: Wipro Appoints Ujjwal Jyoti to Lead Global GCC Practice as AI-Era Demand Surges
excerpt: The former Accenture managing director returns to Wipro as SVP to drive the company strategy for building and transforming enterprise Global Capability Centres.
body:
• Wipro has appointed Ujjwal Jyoti as Senior Vice President and Global GCC Practice Lead, bringing over two decades of experience across consulting and technology delivery
  • Jyoti returns to Wipro after serving as Managing Director and Partner at Accenture, where he led consulting and enterprise transformation initiatives
  • The appointment signals the intensifying competition among Indian IT majors to capture the growing Global Capability Centre market as enterprises invest in AI-native operations
  • TCS, Infosys, and HCL Technologies have all made similar leadership moves in recent months as GCCs evolve from cost-focused delivery hubs into strategic innovation platforms

A Strategic Hire for an Expanding Market

Wipro has appointed Ujjwal Jyoti as Senior Vice President and Global GCC Practice Lead, the company announced, in a move aimed at strengthening its position in the fast-growing market for Global Capability Centre services.

https://x.com/Apacnewsnetwork/status/2097216727545426203

Jyoti will lead Wipro's global GCC practice with a mandate focused on helping clients develop technology and business operations aligned with their transformation priorities, according to APAC Media, which first reported the appointment.

The appointment comes just over a year after Wipro hired Sandeep Dhar as Global Head of its GCC practice in May 2025, suggesting the company is deepening its bench in a segment it sees as critical to future growth.

From Accenture Back to Wipro

Jyoti returns to Wipro after serving as Managing Director and Partner at Accenture, where he worked on consulting and enterprise transformation initiatives. He previously held a programme director role at Wipro earlier in his career.

His professional journey spans leadership and technology delivery roles at DXC Technology, where he served as Delivery Manager, and Tech Mahindra, where he began his career as a software engineer. His experience covers GCC strategy, programme management, technology transformation, and global delivery.

"GCCs have become an important part of enterprise strategy, moving beyond traditional delivery models to support innovation, transformation and specialised capabilities."

— Ujjwal Jyoti, SVP and Global GCC Practice Lead, Wipro

The GCC Land Grab Among Indian IT Majors

Wipro's appointment reflects a broader scramble among India's top IT services companies to capture the growing GCC market. In June 2026, Tata Consultancy Services launched its Global Value and Innovation Centres unit and appointed Soumen Roy, formerly Country Head for TCS Canada, to lead the business. TCS said it works with more than 150 global enterprises on building and managing GCCs.

The rush to hire GCC-focused leadership stems from a fundamental shift in how multinational companies view their offshore centres. What were once cost-reduction hubs focused on back-office IT support are increasingly being repositioned as strategic assets that own products, platforms, and business outcomes. AI adoption has accelerated this evolution, with enterprises looking to embed machine learning and automation into GCC operations from the ground up.

India remains the dominant destination for GCCs, with over 1,700 centres operating across the country, according to industry estimates. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune account for the bulk of operations, though newer centres are expanding into tier-two cities.

What Is at Stake for Wipro

For Wipro, the GCC practice represents an opportunity to deepen client relationships beyond traditional outsourcing contracts. Rather than competing purely on hourly rates for IT services, building and managing GCCs allows firms like Wipro to position themselves as strategic transformation partners.

The company has described its approach as consulting-led and AI-powered, designed to help enterprises establish and scale GCCs as future-ready transformation and innovation hubs.

Looking Ahead

Jyoti's appointment comes amid growing enterprise focus on GCCs as organisations expand global centres to support digital transformation, innovation, and access to specialised talent. With Indian IT majors stacking their leadership benches in this space, the competition for large GCC transformation contracts is expected to intensify through 2027.
